questions.q: For about how long has the Crown been a symbol of the state in Canada?
questions.e: The Crown has been a symbol of the state in Canada for 400 years.

questions.q: Canada has been a monarchy since the time of the early French and English explorers.
questions.e: Canada has been a monarchy in its own right since Confederation in 1867, and before that under the Crowns of France and England.

questions.q: In which year was the current Canadian flag (the red and white maple leaf flag) first raised?
questions.e: A new Canadian flag was raised for the first time in 1965.

The flag of the United States

questions.q: Since when have red and white been the official colours of Canada?
questions.e: Red and white have been the official colours of Canada since 1921.

questions.q: The Union Jack is Canada's official Royal Union Flag.
questions.e: The Union Jack is our official Royal Flag. The Canadian Red Ensign served as the Canadian flag for about 100 years.

questions.q: Each province and territory has its own flag.
questions.e: The provinces and territories also have flags that embody their distinct traditions.

questions.q: What is Canada's best-known symbol?
questions.e: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol. Maple leaves have been on Canadian uniforms and insignia since the 1850s.

questions.q: Who adopted the maple leaf as a symbol in the 1700s?
questions.e: The maple leaf was adopted as a symbol by French Canadians in the 1700s. It has appeared on Canadian uniforms and insignia since the 1850s and is carved into the headstones of fallen soldiers.

questions.q: The maple leaf is carved into the headstones of Canadian soldiers buried overseas.
questions.e: The maple leaf has been carved into the headstones of fallen soldiers buried overseas and in Canada.

questions.q: What does the fleur-de-lys represent?
questions.a: It is a lily flower, a symbol of the French monarchy for more than 1,000 years
w: It is the symbol of the British Royal Navy
It is an Aboriginal symbol of the North
It is a symbol of the Canadian Pacific Railway
questions.e: The lily flower (fleur-de-lys) was adopted by the French king in the year 496. It became a symbol of French royalty for more than 1,000 years.

questions.q: Which province's flag is based on the cross and the fleur-de-lys?
questions.e: Quebec's flag, adopted in 1948, is based on the cross and the fleur-de-lys.

questions.q: What is Canada's motto?
questions.a: A mari usque ad mare (From sea to sea)
questions.e: Canada's motto, 'A mari usque ad mare', means 'from sea to sea' in Latin.

questions.q: What does 'A mari usque ad mare' mean?
questions.e: 'A mari usque ad mare' is Latin for 'from sea to sea'. It appears on Canada's coat of arms.

questions.q: The arms of Canada include symbols of which countries?
questions.e: The arms contain symbols of England, France, Scotland and Ireland, as well as red maple leaves.

questions.q: Which tower of the Parliament Buildings was built in memory of the First World War?
questions.e: The Peace Tower was completed in 1927 in memory of the First World War.

questions.q: What is kept in the Memorial Chamber of the Peace Tower?
questions.a: The Books of Remembrance with the names of soldiers who died serving Canada
questions.e: The Memorial Chamber within the Peace Tower contains the Books of Remembrance, in which are written the names of soldiers, sailors and airmen who died serving Canada.

questions.q: The Parliament Buildings in Ottawa are an example of Gothic Revival architecture.
questions.e: The Parliament Buildings embody the French, English and Aboriginal traditions and are built in the Gothic Revival style.

questions.q: What is Canada's national winter sport?
questions.e: Hockey is Canada's most popular spectator sport and is considered to be the national winter sport.

questions.q: What is Canada's official summer sport?
questions.e: Lacrosse, an ancient sport first played by Aboriginal people, is Canada's official summer sport.

questions.q: What is the name of the trophy for the best hockey team in North America, donated by a Governor General in 1892?
questions.e: The Stanley Cup, donated by Lord Stanley, the Governor General, in 1892, is the championship trophy of professional hockey.

questions.q: Which sport has the largest number of registered players in Canada?
questions.e: Soccer has the largest number of registered players of any game in Canada.

questions.q: Which winter sport was brought to Canada by Scottish pioneers?
questions.e: Curling, an ice game introduced by Scottish pioneers, is popular in Canada.

questions.q: Lacrosse was first played by Aboriginal people.
questions.e: Lacrosse is an ancient sport first played by Aboriginal people. It is Canada's official summer sport.

questions.q: Which animal is an official symbol of Canada and appears on the five-cent coin?
questions.e: The beaver was adopted centuries ago as a symbol of the Hudson's Bay Company. It became an emblem of the St-Jean-Baptiste Society in 1834 and appears on the five-cent coin.

questions.q: Which company adopted the beaver as a symbol centuries ago?
questions.e: The beaver was adopted centuries ago as a symbol of the Hudson's Bay Company, because of the fur trade.

questions.q: What is the national anthem of Canada?
questions.e: 'O Canada' was proclaimed as the national anthem in 1980.

questions.q: When was 'O Canada' proclaimed as the national anthem?
questions.e: 'O Canada' was proclaimed as the national anthem in 1980. It was first sung in Quebec City in 1880.

questions.e: 'O Canada' was first sung in Quebec City in 1880.

questions.q: What is the Royal Anthem of Canada?
questions.e: The Royal Anthem of Canada, 'God Save the King' (or Queen), can be played or sung on any occasion when Canadians wish to honour the Sovereign.

questions.q: Which line is part of the English words of 'O Canada'?
w: Land of the free and home of the brave
From the mountains to the prairies
questions.e: 'O Canada! Our home and native land! True patriot love in all of us command…'

questions.q: What is the highest honour available to Canadians for bravery in war?
questions.e: The Victoria Cross (V.C.) is the highest honour available to Canadians. It is awarded for the most conspicuous bravery, a daring act of valour or self-sacrifice, or extreme devotion to duty in the presence of the enemy.

questions.q: How many Canadians have been awarded the Victoria Cross since 1854?
questions.e: Ninety-six Canadians have been awarded the Victoria Cross since 1854.

questions.q: Who was the first Canadian to be awarded the Victoria Cross, for the Charge of the Light Brigade in 1854?
questions.e: Lieutenant Alexander Roberts Dunn, born in Toronto, served in the Charge of the Light Brigade during the Crimean War (1854) and was the first Canadian to be awarded the Victoria Cross.

questions.q: Who was the first Black man to be awarded the Victoria Cross?
questions.e: Able Seaman William Hall of Horton Bluff, Nova Scotia, whose parents were American slaves, was the first Black man to be awarded the Victoria Cross, for his role in the Indian Rebellion in 1857.

questions.q: Which Ukrainian-born Canadian soldier was awarded the Victoria Cross in 1917?
questions.e: Corporal Filip Konowal, born in Ukraine, showed exceptional courage in 1917 and was awarded the Victoria Cross.

questions.q: Who was the navy pilot who was the last Canadian to receive the Victoria Cross?
questions.e: Lieutenant Robert Hampton Gray, a navy pilot from British Columbia, died in 1945 attacking a Japanese warship. He was the last Canadian to receive the Victoria Cross to date.

questions.q: Which honour was created in 1967, Canada's centennial, to recognize outstanding Canadians?
questions.e: In 1967, Canada's centennial year, the Order of Canada was established. It is the country's highest honour for lifetime achievement.

questions.q: On which date is Canada Day?
questions.e: Canada Day, July 1, celebrates the anniversary of Confederation in 1867.

questions.q: When is Labour Day?
questions.e: Labour Day is the first Monday of September.

questions.q: When is Thanksgiving Day in Canada?

questions.e: Sir John A. Macdonald Day is January 11, his birthday. It is not a public holiday.
